learn.hook: Ring, ring! Who is coming down the lane? It is a happy child on a bicycle!
points: The lesson 'My Bicycle' is a poem about the joy of riding a bicycle.
A poem has short lines. Many lines end with sounds that match.
Read slowly. Think about who, what, where and when.
The answer is often right there in a line of the poem.

example.q:
Read this poem.
My bicycle is red and bright,
I ride it in the morning light.
Ring, ring! goes my little bell,
I wave to Ravi, he waves as well.
Up the lane and round the tree,
My bicycle is fun for me!
When does the child ride the bicycle?
steps: Look for a line about time.
Line 2 says: 'I ride it in the morning light.'
So the child rides in the morning.

learn.reallife: When you read a story book or a sign on the road, you look for who, what and where, just like this.

games.title: Poem in order
games.prompt: Put the poem lines in the right order
items: My bicycle is red and bright,
I ride it in the morning light.
Ring, ring! goes my little bell,
I wave to Ravi, he waves as well.

games.title: True or false? (about the poem)
items: In the poem, the bicycle is red.
The poem says: 'My bicycle is red and bright.'
In the poem, the child rides at night.
The poem says the child rides in the morning light.
In the poem, the bell goes ring, ring.
The poem says: 'Ring, ring! goes my little bell.'
In the poem, Ravi runs away.
Ravi waves back. He does not run away.
In the poem, the child rides round a tree.
The poem says: 'Up the lane and round the tree.'

quiz.q: Poem line: 'My bicycle is red and bright.' What colour is the bicycle?
quiz.explain: The line says the bicycle is red and bright.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a colour without reading the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Ring, ring! goes my little bell.' What goes ring, ring?
quiz.explain: The line says 'my little bell' goes ring, ring.
quiz.mistake: Picks another part of the bicycle without reading carefully

quiz.q: Poem line: 'I wave to Ravi, he waves as well.' What does Ravi do?
quiz.explain: 'He waves as well' means Ravi also waves.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that 'as well' means 'also'

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Up the lane and round the tree.' What does the child ride round?
quiz.explain: The line says the child rides round the tree.
quiz.mistake: Picks a place that is not in the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'My bicycle is fun for me!' How does the child feel?
quiz.explain: Fun things make us happy. The child enjoys the bicycle.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the word 'fun' with feeling happy

quiz.q: What is the lesson 'My Bicycle' mainly about?
quiz.explain: The poem talks about the joy of riding a bicycle.
quiz.mistake: Does not look at the title to find the main idea

teach.ask: Gappu: I read a poem but I can't find the answers! How do I find them?
teach.praise: Yay! I read the poem slowly and find the line with the answer. Easy!
teach.nudge: Should I read the poem again? Where in the poem is the answer hiding?

learn.hook: Cat, hat, mat, bat! Why do these words sound like a song?
points: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
bright and light rhyme. bell and well rhyme.
Only the first sound changes: c-at, h-at, m-at.
Poems often use rhyming words at the end of lines.

example.q: Which word rhymes with 'ride': slide or ring?
steps: Say the end sound of ride: -ide.
slide ends with -ide too.
ring ends with -ing. That is different.

learn.reallife: Many songs and nursery rhymes you sing in school use rhyming words.

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'bike'?
quiz.explain: bike and like both end with the -ike sound.
quiz.mistake: Matches only the first letter instead of the end sound

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'wheel'?
quiz.explain: wheel and seal both end with the -eel sound.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the first letter 'w' instead of the end sound

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'ring'?
quiz.explain: ring and sing both end with the -ing sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that starts the same, not one that ends the same

quiz.q: Which pair of words rhymes?
quiz.explain: cat and mat both end with -at. The other pairs only start the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words that start the same are rhyming words

quiz.q: Which word does NOT rhyme with 'tree'?
quiz.explain: tray ends with an -ay sound. tree, bee, see and knee end with -ee.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the first letters 'tr' and thinks tray must rhyme

quiz.q: Rhyming words have the same ___ at the end.
quiz.explain: Rhyming is about sound. bell and well sound the same at the end.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that rhyming is about sounds

teach.ask: Gappu: My teacher says 'cat' and 'hat' rhyme. What does rhyme mean?
teach.praise: Now I know! Rhyming words sound the same at the end. Bat, rat, mat!
teach.nudge: Is it the start or the end of the words that sounds the same?

learn.hook: A bicycle has many parts. Can you name them all?
points: A bicycle has two wheels. 'Bi' means two.
We push the pedals with our feet. We turn the handlebar to steer.
We press the brakes to stop. We ring the bell to warn people.
Wear a helmet. Ride where an adult says it is safe.

example.q: Meena sees a dog on the path ahead. Which part should she use to stop?
steps: The bell only makes a sound.
The pedals make the bicycle go.
The brakes make the bicycle stop.

learn.reallife: When you ride in your colony park, you ring the bell and use the brakes to keep everyone safe.

items.text: I wear a ___ on my head.
I ring the ___ to say 'Move, please!'

quiz.q: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
quiz.explain: A bicycle has two wheels. 'Bi' means two.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a bicycle with a tricycle or a car

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct?
quiz.explain: We spell it b-i-c-y-c-l-e.
quiz.mistake: Writes the word the way it sounds, not the way it is spelt

quiz.q: Which thing keeps your head safe when you ride?
quiz.explain: A helmet is hard and strong. It protects your head if you fall.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any head cover keeps you safe

quiz.q: Which part do you push with your feet to make the bicycle go?
quiz.explain: Your feet push the pedals round and the wheels move.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of bicycle parts

quiz.q: Kabir wants to turn left on his bicycle. What does he turn?
quiz.explain: We turn the handlebar to steer the bicycle left or right.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pedals or brakes help to steer

quiz.q: Which is a safe thing to do on a bicycle?
options: Ring the bell to warn people
Ride on a busy road alone
quiz.explain: Ringing the bell tells people you are coming. The others can cause a fall.
quiz.mistake: Thinks showing off on a bicycle is safe

teach.ask: Gappu: I got a new bicycle! How do I ride it safely?
teach.praise: Thank you! Helmet on, bell to warn, brakes to stop. I am a safe rider now!
teach.nudge: What do I wear on my head? And how do I stop or warn people?

learn.hook: A picture can tell a whole story without a single word. Let's read one!
points: The lesson 'Picture Reading' asks us to look at a picture and talk about it.
Ask: Who is there? What are they doing? Where are they?
Look for colours, numbers and small details.
Then say it in short sentences.

example.q:
Imagine this park picture.
In the park, Arjun flies a yellow kite.
Two girls swing high on the swings.
A brown dog runs after a ball.
Dadi sits on a bench and smiles.
Who is sitting on the bench?
steps: Find the line about the bench.
It says: 'Dadi sits on a bench and smiles.'
So Dadi is on the bench.

learn.reallife: When you tell Mummy about your school trip, you are describing a scene.

games.title: Check the park picture
items: In the park picture, Arjun flies a yellow kite.
The scene says: 'Arjun flies a yellow kite.'
In the park picture, three girls are on the swings.
The scene says two girls swing on the swings.
In the park picture, the dog is brown.
The scene says: 'A brown dog runs after a ball.'
In the park picture, Dadi is crying.
Dadi sits on a bench and smiles.
In the park picture, the dog runs after a ball.
The scene says the dog runs after a ball.

quiz.q: Scene: 'Arjun flies a yellow kite.' What colour is the kite?
quiz.explain: The scene says the kite is yellow.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for the colour word

quiz.q: Scene: 'Two girls swing high on the swings.' How many girls are on the swings?
quiz.explain: The word 'two' tells us there are 2 girls.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the number word 'two'

quiz.q: Scene: 'A brown dog runs after a ball.' What does the dog run after?
quiz.explain: The scene says the dog runs after a ball.
quiz.mistake: Guesses what dogs usually chase instead of reading

quiz.q: In 'Arjun flies a kite in the park', which words tell WHERE?
quiz.explain: 'In the park' tells us the place. That answers 'where?'
quiz.mistake: Mixes up who, what and where

quiz.q: Which sentence describes a market scene?
options: A baby sleeps in a cot.
quiz.explain: In a market, people buy and sell things like fruits and vegetables.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about what is seen in a market

quiz.q: Which question helps you find WHO is in a picture?
quiz.explain: 'Who' asks about people or animals in the picture.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the question words who, where and what

teach.ask: Gappu: My teacher showed a picture and said 'Tell me about it.' What do I say?
teach.praise: Super! I say who is there, what they are doing and where they are!
teach.nudge: Should I tell who is in the picture? What about what they are doing and where?

learn.hook: Run! Jump! Clap! Can you do these right now?
points: An action word tells what someone or something does.
run, jump, eat, sing, write and swim are action words.
Action words are also called doing words.
In 'Riya kicks the ball', the action word is 'kicks'.

example.q: Find the action word: 'The baby claps.'
steps: Ask: What does the baby do?
The baby claps.
So 'claps' is the action word.

learn.reallife: In PT class, your teacher calls out action words: run, stop, jump, bend!

quiz.q: Which one is an action word?
quiz.explain: We can jump. It is something we do.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any word is an action word

quiz.q: Find the action word: 'Riya kicks the ball.'
quiz.explain: 'Kicks' tells what Riya does.
quiz.mistake: Picks the name of the person or thing instead of the action

quiz.q: Which action word fits? 'Birds ___ in the sky.'
quiz.explain: Birds fly in the sky.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about what makes sense in the sentence

quiz.q: Find the action word: 'Dadi cooks dal.'
quiz.explain: 'Cooks' tells what Dadi does.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word, or a word not in the sentence

quiz.q: Which word is NOT an action word?
quiz.explain: A cup is a thing. We cannot 'cup'. sing, dance and read are actions.
quiz.mistake: Does not tell things apart from actions

quiz.q: Action words are also called ___ words.
quiz.explain: Action words tell what we do, so they are called doing words.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up doing words with naming or describing words

teach.ask: Gappu: What is an action word? Is 'banana' an action word?
teach.praise: Hop hop! An action word tells what we do, like jump or sing. Banana is not one!
teach.nudge: Does an action word tell what we do? Can you give me an example?

learn.hook: Words are like beads. Put them in the right order to make a sentence necklace!
points: A sentence tells a full idea.
A sentence begins with a capital letter.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.).
Words must be in the right order to make sense.

example.q: Put the words in order: dog / The / fast. / runs
steps: Start with the word that has a capital letter: The.
Who? dog. What does it do? runs. How? fast.
The full stop comes at the end.

learn.reallife: When you write in your notebook, your teacher checks for capital letters and full stops.

games.title: Make a sentence
games.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence

games.title: Sentence rules
items: A sentence begins with a capital letter.
We always begin a sentence with a capital letter.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.).
'dog the runs' is a good sentence.
The words are mixed up. It should be 'The dog runs.'
'a big red' is a full sentence.
It does not tell a full idea. Big red what? What happens?
'Sita plays with a top.' is a sentence.
It begins with a capital letter, ends with a full stop and tells a full idea.

quiz.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
quiz.explain: It begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the capital letter or the full stop

quiz.q: Which word order makes a sentence?
quiz.explain: 'The cat drinks milk.' makes sense. The others are mixed up.
quiz.mistake: Does not check if the words make sense in that order

quiz.q: What comes at the end of a telling sentence?
quiz.explain: A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the full stop with other marks

quiz.q: Which word should begin with a capital letter? 'my dog is brown.'
quiz.explain: 'my' is the first word of the sentence, so it needs a capital M.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the first word of a sentence takes a capital letter

quiz.q: Picture: a boy is drinking water. Which sentence matches?
quiz.explain: It says the right person (boy) and the right action (drinks water).
quiz.mistake: Matches only part of the picture

quiz.q: Which one is a full sentence?
quiz.explain: It tells a full idea: who (Sita) and what she does (plays with a top).
quiz.mistake: Thinks a group of words is always a sentence

teach.ask: Gappu: I wrote 'cat the sleeps'. My teacher says it's not a sentence. Why?
teach.praise: I get it! 'The cat sleeps.' Right order, capital letter and a full stop!
teach.nudge: Are my words in the right order? How should a sentence begin and end?

topics.title: A poem about play and nature

learn.hook: Sun, trees, puddles and butterflies! What makes playing outside so much fun?
points: The lesson 'It is Fun' is a poem about the fun of play. Our own poem here is about playing outside in nature.
Nature means things not made by people: trees, sun, rain, birds and flowers.
Poems can use the same words again and again, like 'It is fun to...'.
Read each line and picture it in your mind.

example.q:
Read this poem.
It is fun to run in the sun,
It is fun to rest under a tree,
It is fun to hop in the puddles,
And watch a butterfly, free.
Playing out with friends all day
Is the best fun for you and me!
What does the child hop in?
steps: Find the line with 'hop'.
It says: 'It is fun to hop in the puddles.'
So the child hops in the puddles.

learn.reallife: After the rain, children love to jump in puddles and watch butterflies in the garden.

items.text: It is fun to run in the ___.
It is fun to rest under a ___.
It is fun to hop in the ___.

quiz.q: Poem line: 'It is fun to rest under a tree.' Where does the child rest?
quiz.explain: The line says the child rests under a tree.
quiz.mistake: Picks a usual resting place instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'And watch a butterfly, free.' What does the child watch?
quiz.explain: The line says the child watches a butterfly.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without reading the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'It is fun to run in the sun.' Which word rhymes with 'run'?
quiz.explain: run and fun both end with the -un sound. (sun rhymes too!)
quiz.mistake: Picks any word from the line, not one that sounds the same at the end

quiz.q: Which of these is a part of nature?
quiz.explain: A tree grows on its own. Phones, cars and TVs are made by people.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that nature means things not made by people

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Playing out with friends all day.' Who does the child play with?
quiz.explain: The line says 'with friends'.
quiz.mistake: Does not read who is in the line

quiz.q: Our poem says 'It is fun to run in the sun' and 'hop in the puddles'. What is our poem mainly about?
quiz.explain: The poem talks about playing outside with trees, sun and butterflies.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the main idea of the whole poem

teach.ask: Gappu: Why is it fun to play outside? What is nature?
teach.praise: Wow! Nature is trees, sun and birds, and playing there is great fun!
teach.nudge: What things are part of nature? What can we do outside?

learn.hook: Look! The puppy is running, the baby is smiling and Dadi is singing!
points: Doing words tell what someone does: run, hop, sing, climb.
We can add -ing to show what is happening now: play → playing.
Some words change a little: run → running, dance → dancing.
We say 'is' for one and 'are' for many: 'The girl is playing.' 'The boys are playing.'

example.q: Choose the right word: 'Look! The baby is ___.' (smiling / smile)
steps: After 'is' we use the -ing word to show what is happening now.
'The baby is smiling.' sounds right.

learn.reallife: When you tell your friend 'I am drawing' or 'We are playing', you use doing words.

items.text: The cat is ___ on the mat.

quiz.q: Find the doing word: 'The children play in the park.'
quiz.explain: 'Play' tells what the children do.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word instead of the doing word

quiz.q: Which -ing word is spelt correctly?
quiz.explain: run becomes running. We write one more n before -ing.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the n in running

quiz.q: Which doing word goes best with 'a kite'?
quiz.explain: We fly a kite. We do not eat, drink or sleep a kite!
quiz.mistake: Does not check if the action makes sense with the thing

quiz.q: Which word is a doing word?
quiz.explain: We can climb. Tree and sun are things. Happy is a feeling.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up doing words with naming or describing words

quiz.q: Choose the right word: 'The ducks ___ swimming in the pond.'
quiz.explain: Ducks means many, so we use 'are'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'is' for more than one

quiz.q: What is the -ing word for 'dance'?
quiz.explain: We drop the e and add -ing: dancing.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the e before adding -ing

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend said 'I am jumping.' Which one is the doing word?
teach.praise: Yes! 'Jumping' is the doing word. It tells what my friend is doing!
teach.nudge: Which word tells what my friend is doing?

learn.hook: The swing goes up... and down! Up and down are opposites.
points: Opposite words mean very different things.
up – down, fast – slow, hot – cold, wet – dry.
big – small, day – night, happy – sad, open – close.
Opposites help us compare two things.

example.q: Rohan runs fast. His little brother runs ___. Pick the opposite of 'fast'.
steps: Fast means very quick.
The opposite of quick is not quick.
That word is 'slow'.

learn.reallife: At the park, the slide takes you down and the steps take you up.

games.title: Opposite or not?
items: Fast is quick, slow is not quick. They are opposites.
Big and large mean the same thing.
In and out mean very different places.
Happy and glad mean the same thing.
You open a door to go out and close it after.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'open'?
quiz.explain: We open a box and then close it. They are opposites.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word linked to doors instead of the opposite

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'fast'?
quiz.explain: Fast means quick. Slow means not quick.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with the same meaning instead of the opposite

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'wet'?
quiz.explain: Wet clothes have water. Dry clothes have no water.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word linked to water instead of the opposite

quiz.q: The sun shines in the day. The moon shines at ___.
quiz.explain: Day and night are opposites. We see the moon at night.
quiz.mistake: Picks another time of the day

quiz.q: Which pair of words are opposites?
quiz.explain: Big and small mean very different things. The other pairs mean almost the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words with similar meanings are opposites

quiz.q: The see-saw goes up and ___.
quiz.explain: One end goes up and the other end goes down.
quiz.mistake: Does not think of the opposite of up

teach.ask: Gappu: What does 'opposite' mean? What is the opposite of 'hot'?
teach.praise: Brrr! Hot and cold are opposites. They mean very different things!
teach.nudge: Do opposite words mean the same or very different things? What is the opposite of hot?

learn.hook: Close your eyes. Can you still know what is around you? Yes, you can!
points: The lesson 'Seeing without Seeing' is about knowing the world without using our eyes.
We have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
Eyes see. Ears hear. Nose smells. Tongue tastes. Skin feels.
When we cannot see, the other senses help us a lot.

example.q: Your eyes are shut. You hear 'Moo!' Which sense helps you know a cow is near?
steps: 'Moo' is a sound.
We hear sounds with our ears.
So hearing tells us a cow is near.

learn.reallife: In the dark at night, you know Mummy is near when you hear her voice.

quiz.q: We hear with our ___.
quiz.explain: Ears catch sounds. That is how we hear.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the body parts and their senses

quiz.q: Which part of the body helps you taste food?
quiz.explain: The tongue tells us if food is sweet, sour or salty.
quiz.mistake: Does not link taste with the tongue

quiz.q: How many senses do we have?
quiz.explain: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. That is five.
quiz.mistake: Forgets one or more senses

quiz.q: Which sense tells you that a rose smells nice?
quiz.explain: We smell with our nose.
quiz.mistake: Thinks we know a smell by seeing the flower

quiz.q: You touch a cat's fur with your eyes shut. Which sense are you using?
quiz.explain: We feel things with our skin. That is the sense of touch.
quiz.mistake: Thinks we need to see to know a thing

quiz.q: The pressure cooker whistles. Which sense tells you this?
quiz.explain: A whistle is a sound. We hear it with our ears.
quiz.mistake: Picks smell because the cooker is in the kitchen

teach.ask: Gappu: If I close my eyes, how can I know what is around me?
teach.praise: Wow! I can hear with my ears, smell with my nose and feel with my hands!
teach.nudge: Which other senses can I use? What can my ears, nose and hands do?

topics.title: Words for sounds, smells, tastes and touch

learn.hook: Is it sweet or sour? Soft or rough? Let's find words for what we feel!
points: Taste words: sweet, sour, salty, bitter.
Touch words: soft, hard, rough, smooth, hot, cold.
Sound words: loud, soft, quiet.
These words help us describe things even with our eyes shut.

example.q:
Read this.
Tara closes her eyes.
She hears a whistle. It is the pressure cooker!
She smells hot pakoras.
She touches her cat. It is soft.
She tastes a sweet laddoo. Yum!
Which sense tells Tara about the pakoras?
steps: Find the line about pakoras.
It says: 'She smells hot pakoras.'
We smell with our nose.

learn.reallife: When you eat a lemon or touch a smooth stone, you use these words to tell your friends.

quiz.q: Passage: 'She hears a whistle. It is the pressure cooker!' What makes the whistle?
quiz.explain: The passage says the whistle is the pressure cooker.
quiz.mistake: Guesses something else that whistles

quiz.q: Passage: 'She touches her cat. It is soft.' How does the cat feel?
quiz.explain: The passage says the cat is soft.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the describing word in the line

quiz.q: Passage: 'She tastes a sweet laddoo.' How does the laddoo taste?
quiz.explain: The passage says it is a sweet laddoo.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the taste word in the line

quiz.q: Which word tells how a lemon tastes?
quiz.explain: A lemon makes your mouth pucker. It tastes sour.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up taste words

quiz.q: How does the bark of an old tree feel?
quiz.explain: Tree bark has bumps and cracks. It feels rough.
quiz.mistake: Uses a taste or sound word for touch

quiz.q: Which one is a sound word?
quiz.explain: Loud tells us about a sound, like a drum or thunder.
quiz.mistake: Does not tell sound words apart from taste or touch words

teach.ask: Gappu: I ate a lemon with my eyes shut! What word tells how it tasted?
teach.praise: Ooh! The lemon tasted sour. My tongue told me, even with my eyes shut!
teach.nudge: Was the lemon sweet or sour? Which part of me tasted it?

topics.title: Being kind to people who cannot see

learn.hook: Can you read a book with your fingers? Some people do it every day!
points: Some people cannot see. We say they are visually impaired.
Many of them read Braille. Braille has tiny raised dots that you feel with your fingers.
Louis Braille made this way of reading. He could not see either.
A white cane helps a person feel the path ahead.
To help, first ask kindly: 'May I help you?' Tell them your name when you talk.

example.q:
Read this.
Aman cannot see.
He reads with his fingers.
His book has tiny raised dots.
He walks with a white cane.
He loves music and chess.
How does Aman read his book?
steps: Find the line about reading.
It says: 'He reads with his fingers.'
The raised dots are Braille.

learn.reallife: Many lift buttons have raised dots next to the numbers so people who cannot see can use them.

games.title: Kind or not?
items: Many people who cannot see read using Braille.
Braille dots are felt with the fingers.
It is kind to ask 'May I help you?' before helping.
We should pull a person who cannot see to help them walk.
Pulling can scare them. Ask first and let them hold your arm.
A white cane helps a person feel the way.
The cane touches the ground ahead and finds steps and bumps.
People who cannot see cannot enjoy music.
They can hear music and enjoy it, just like you.

quiz.q: Passage: 'His book has tiny raised dots.' What are these dots called?
quiz.explain: Raised dots that people read with their fingers are called Braille.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word Braille

quiz.q: Passage: 'He walks with a white cane.' How does the cane help Aman?
quiz.explain: The cane touches the ground ahead and finds steps and bumps.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a white cane is for

quiz.q: Passage: 'He loves music and chess.' What does Aman love?
quiz.explain: The passage says he loves music and chess.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Who made the Braille way of reading?
quiz.explain: Braille is named after Louis Braille, who made it.
quiz.mistake: Picks a famous name without linking it to Braille

quiz.q: You see a person with a white cane at a step. What should you do first?
quiz.explain: Asking first is polite. They can tell you how to help.
quiz.mistake: Helps without asking, which can scare the person

quiz.q: You meet a friend who cannot see. What is a kind thing to do?
options: Tell your name when you speak
quiz.explain: They cannot see your face, so telling your name helps them know you.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the friend cannot see a wave or a face

teach.ask: Gappu: My new friend Zoya cannot see. How can I be a good friend to her?
teach.praise: Lovely! I will ask before I help, tell her my name and always be kind.
teach.nudge: Should I ask before I help? How will Zoya know it is me?

topics.title: A poem about a friend going away

learn.hook: Your best friend is going away for the holidays. What will you say?
points: The lesson 'Come Back Soon' is a poem about going away on a trip and coming back soon. Our own poem here is about a friend going away.
When a friend goes away, we miss them.
We say goodbye and hope to meet again soon.
Look for feeling words in a poem. They tell us how someone feels.

example.q:
Read this poem.
My friend Neha goes away today,
To her nani's house for a holiday.
I wave my hand and say goodbye,
A little tear comes to my eye.
'Come back soon, we'll play again!
We'll swing and sing in the summer rain!'
Where is Neha going?
steps: Find the line about where Neha goes.
It says: 'To her nani's house for a holiday.'
So Neha is going to her nani's house.

learn.reallife: In the summer holidays, many friends go to their grandparents' homes. We wave goodbye and wait for them.

games.title: What happens next?
items: Neha says she is going away.
Neha stays at her nani's house.
Neha comes back and they play again.

games.title: True or false? (about the poem)
items: In the poem, Neha goes to her nani's house.
The poem says: 'To her nani's house for a holiday.'
In the poem, the child laughs at Neha.
The child waves goodbye and feels a little sad.
In the poem, a tear comes to the child's eye.
The poem says: 'A little tear comes to my eye.'
In the poem, the child wants Neha to come back soon.
The child says: 'Come back soon, we'll play again!'
In the poem, Neha goes away to school.
She goes to her nani's house for a holiday.

quiz.q: Poem line: 'A little tear comes to my eye.' How does the child feel?
quiz.explain: Tears often come when we are sad. The child will miss Neha.
quiz.mistake: Does not link a tear with feeling sad

quiz.q: Poem line: 'I wave my hand and say goodbye.' What does the child do?
quiz.explain: The line says the child waves a hand and says goodbye.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the action in the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'My friend Neha goes away today.' Who is Neha?
quiz.explain: The line says 'My friend Neha'.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without reading the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Come back soon, we'll play again!' What does the child hope?
options: Neha comes back and they play
quiz.explain: The child wants Neha to come back so they can play again.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the words 'come back soon'

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'goodbye'?
quiz.explain: goodbye and eye both end with the same 'eye' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from the poem that does not sound the same at the end

quiz.q: Poem line: 'To her nani's house for a holiday.' Who is Neha going to meet?
quiz.explain: Nani is Neha's grandmother. She is going to nani's house.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that nani means grandmother

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend is going away for a holiday. What should I say to her?
teach.praise: That is so sweet! 'Goodbye! Come back soon!' My friend will feel loved.
teach.nudge: What do we say when someone leaves? And what do we hope they will do?

learn.hook: Smiles, tears, frowns and giggles! Our faces show how we feel.
points: Feeling words tell how we feel inside.
happy, sad, angry, scared, excited, proud, surprised.
When a friend goes away, we may feel sad. When they come back, we feel happy.
All feelings are okay. It helps to talk about them.

example.q: Kiran wins the drawing prize at school. Which feeling word fits best?
steps: Winning a prize is a good thing.
We feel good about what we did.
That feeling is called proud.

learn.reallife: When you tell Papa 'I am scared of the thunder', he knows how to help you.

quiz.q: Ravi gets a new puppy. How does he feel?
quiz.explain: A new puppy is a lovely thing. Ravi feels happy.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how the event would feel

quiz.q: Meera's best friend moves to another city. How does Meera feel?
quiz.explain: She will miss her friend, so she feels sad.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about missing a friend

quiz.q: There is a loud thunder at night. Chotu hides under his blanket. How does he feel?
quiz.explain: Hiding from a loud noise shows Chotu is scared.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue 'hides' to find the feeling

quiz.q: Tomorrow is the school picnic! Anu can't wait. How does she feel?
quiz.explain: 'Can't wait' means she is very excited.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'can't wait'

quiz.q: Someone takes your pencil without asking. You may feel ___.
quiz.explain: Taking things without asking is not nice. It can make us upset.
quiz.mistake: Does not link an unfair act with feeling upset

quiz.q: Kiran opens a box and finds a gift she did not expect! How does she feel?
quiz.explain: When something happens that we did not expect, we feel surprised.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'surprised'

teach.ask: Gappu: I feel funny inside when my friend goes away. What is that feeling called?
teach.praise: Aww. That feeling is sad. I miss my friend. It's okay to feel sad sometimes.
teach.nudge: What is the name of the feeling when we miss someone?

learn.hook: Magic words open hearts! Do you know them?
points: We say 'Hello' or 'Good morning' when we meet someone.
We say 'Goodbye', 'Bye' or 'See you soon' when we leave.
'Please', 'Thank you' and 'Sorry' are kind words.
We say 'Good night' before we sleep.

example.q: Ali's cousin is going back home on the train. What can Ali say?
steps: The cousin is leaving.
We wish people well when they leave.
Ali can say: 'Goodbye! Have a safe trip!'

learn.reallife: At the end of a school day, you wave and say 'Bye! See you tomorrow!' to your friends.

games.title: What do you say?
pairs: You meet your teacher in the morning

items.text: I am ___ I broke your crayon.

quiz.q: You meet your teacher at school in the morning. What do you say?
quiz.explain: We greet people with 'Good morning' in the morning.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up morning and night greetings

quiz.q: Before you sleep, what do you say to your family?
quiz.explain: We say 'Good night' before going to sleep.
quiz.mistake: Uses a greeting for the wrong time of day

quiz.q: Your friend gives you a birthday card. What do you say?
quiz.explain: We say 'Thank you' when someone gives us something.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when to use 'Thank you'

quiz.q: You step on your friend's foot by mistake. What do you say?
quiz.explain: We say 'Sorry' when we hurt someone by mistake.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when to say 'Sorry'

quiz.q: Which words mean almost the same as 'Goodbye'?
quiz.explain: 'See you later' is said when we leave, just like 'Goodbye'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'Hello' is said when leaving

quiz.q: Your friend is leaving for a trip. What is a kind thing to say?
quiz.explain: Wishing a nice trip shows you care about your friend.
quiz.mistake: Does not choose words that wish the friend well

teach.ask: Gappu: What are magic words? When do I say them?
teach.praise: Magic! 'Please' when I ask, 'Thank you' when I get, 'Sorry' when I make a mistake!
teach.nudge: What do I say when I want something? And when someone helps me?

topics.title: Places on the way to school

learn.hook: What do you see on your way to school every day? Let's take a walk!
points: The lesson 'Between Home and School' is about the places we pass on the way to school.
We may pass shops, a park, a bus stop, a post office or a big tree.
Words like first, next, then and after tell us the order.
Always cross the road at a zebra crossing, holding an adult's hand.

example.q:
Read this.
Every day, Sonu walks to school with Papa.
First, they pass the milk booth.
Next, they cross the road at the zebra crossing.
Then they walk past a big banyan tree.
The school gate is just after the post office.
What do they pass first?
steps: Look for the word 'First'.
It says: 'First, they pass the milk booth.'
So the milk booth comes first.

learn.reallife: You can tell a new friend how to reach your school by naming the places on the way.

games.title: Sonu's walk
games.prompt: Put Sonu's walk in order, from home to school

games.title: Place and what we do there

quiz.q: Passage: 'Next, they cross the road at the zebra crossing.' Where do they cross the road?
options: In the middle of the road
quiz.explain: The passage says they cross at the zebra crossing.
quiz.mistake: Does not read where they cross

quiz.q: Passage: 'Then they walk past a big banyan tree.' Which tree do they pass?
quiz.explain: The passage says 'a big banyan tree'.
quiz.mistake: Picks another tree without reading the line

quiz.q: Passage: 'The school gate is just after the post office.' What comes just before the school gate?
quiz.explain: 'Just after the post office' means they pass the post office and then reach the gate.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the word 'after'

quiz.q: Passage: 'Every day, Sonu walks to school with Papa.' Who walks with Sonu?
quiz.explain: The passage says Sonu walks with Papa.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without reading the line

quiz.q: Where is the safest place to cross a road?
options: At a bend in the road
quiz.explain: Drivers know to stop at a zebra crossing. Cross there with an adult.
quiz.mistake: Thinks running across the road is safe

quiz.q: Which word tells what happens first?
quiz.explain: 'First' tells us what comes before everything else.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up order words

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to walk to your school! What places will I pass on the way?
teach.praise: Now I know the way! First this place, then that one. I won't get lost!
teach.nudge: Which places will I see? Which one comes first and which comes next?

learn.hook: Your friend is lost! Can you tell her the way?
points: Direction words tell us which way to go.
left and right are opposites. 'Turn left' or 'Turn right'.
'Go straight' means keep going ahead. Do not turn.
near means close by. far means a long way off.

example.q: Directions: 'Walk straight. Turn left at the fruit shop. The library is on your right.' Where do you turn?
steps: First you walk straight.
The direction says 'Turn left at the fruit shop'.
So you turn at the fruit shop.
example.answer: At the fruit shop, you turn left

learn.reallife: When an auto driver asks 'Left or right?', you can tell him the way to your house.

items.text: The shop is close by. It is ___.
Nani's village is a long way off. It is ___.

games.title: Direction check
items: Go straight means keep going ahead without turning.
Near is close. Far is a long way off.
It tells us which way to go.
Banana is a fruit. It does not tell us which way to go.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'left'?
quiz.explain: Left and right are the two sides. They are opposites.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that left and right go together

quiz.q: 'Go straight' means you should ___.
quiz.explain: Straight means ahead, with no turning.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'straight'

quiz.q: Directions: 'Walk straight. Turn left at the fruit shop. The library is on your right.' Where is the library?
quiz.explain: The directions say 'The library is on your right'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the turn (left) with the side of the library (right)

quiz.q: Your school is 5 minutes away. Nani's village is 5 hours away. Which is far?
quiz.explain: 5 hours is a long time to travel, so Nani's village is far.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the two travel times

quiz.q: Which one is a direction word?
quiz.explain: 'Left' tells us which way to go.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a direction word is

quiz.q: Directions: 'At the bus stop, turn right.' What should you do at the bus stop?
quiz.explain: The directions say to turn right at the bus stop.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend's house is next to the park. How do I tell someone the way?
teach.praise: Great! Go straight, then turn left or right. Now I can give directions!
teach.nudge: Which words tell the way? Should I go straight or turn?

learn.hook: Where is my school bag? In, on or under the bed?
points: Position words tell us where something is.
in, on, under, behind, in front of, next to, between.
'The cat is under the table' means the cat is below the table.
'Sonu sits between Ravi and Meena' means Ravi is on one side and Meena on the other.

example.q: The pencil is inside the box. Which position word fits? 'The pencil is ___ the box.'
steps: Inside means it is in the box.
The word for inside is 'in'.

learn.reallife: When Mummy asks 'Where are your shoes?', you say 'Under the bed!' That is a position word.

quiz.q: The cup is on top of the table. 'The cup is ___ the table.'
quiz.explain: On top of means 'on'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'on' and 'under'

quiz.q: The cat hides below the bed. 'The cat is ___ the bed.'
quiz.explain: Below means 'under'.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that below means under

quiz.q: Sonu sits between Ravi and Meena. Who sits next to Sonu?
quiz.explain: Between means one is on each side. So both Ravi and Meena are next to Sonu.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that 'between' means one on each side

quiz.q: The tree is at the back of the house. 'The tree is ___ the house.'
quiz.explain: At the back of means 'behind'.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'behind'

quiz.q: Which one is a position word?
quiz.explain: 'Under' tells us where something is.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a position word is

quiz.q: The milk booth is beside the bus stop. 'The milk booth is ___ the bus stop.'
quiz.explain: Beside means 'next to'.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that beside means next to

teach.ask: Gappu: I lost my toy! How can you tell me exactly where it is?
teach.praise: Found it! Your position words told me exactly where it was: under the bed!
teach.nudge: Which words tell where a thing is? Is it in, on or under something?

learn.hook: Honk! Ring! Swish! A town is full of sounds and busy people!
points: The lesson 'This is My Town' is a poem about a town and the places in it.
A town has markets, parks, roads, shops and homes.
Many people work in a town to help us.
Rhyming words make the poem fun to read aloud.

example.q:
Read this poem.
This is my town, so busy and bright,
The market is full from morning to night.
The bus says 'honk', the cycles ring,
In the park the children swing.
The postman brings a letter to me,
I love my town, as you can see!
What does the postman bring?
steps: Find the line with 'postman'.
It says: 'The postman brings a letter to me.'
So he brings a letter.

learn.reallife: Look around your own town or village. What places and helpers do you see?

games.title: True or false? (about the poem)
items: In the poem, the market is full from morning to night.
The poem says: 'The market is full from morning to night.'
In the poem, the bus says 'moo'.
In the poem, the children swing in the park.
The poem says: 'In the park the children swing.'
In the poem, the postman brings a cake.
In the poem, the child loves the town.
The poem says: 'I love my town.'

items.text: This is my town, so busy and ___.
The bus says '___', the cycles ring.
The ___ brings a letter to me.

quiz.q: Poem line: 'The market is full from morning to night.' When is the market full?
quiz.explain: The line says the market is full from morning to night.
quiz.mistake: Reads only part of the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'In the park the children swing.' Where do the children swing?
quiz.explain: The line says the children swing in the park.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the place in the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'The bus says honk, the cycles ring.' What says 'honk'?
quiz.explain: The line says 'The bus says honk'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two sounds in the line

quiz.q: Poem line: 'I love my town, as you can see!' How does the child feel about the town?
quiz.explain: The child says 'I love my town'.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the feeling word 'love'

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'bright'?
quiz.explain: bright and night both end with the -ight sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from the poem that does not rhyme

quiz.q: Poem line: 'In the park the children swing.' Which word rhymes with 'swing'?
quiz.explain: swing and ring both end with the -ing sound.
quiz.mistake: Does not listen to the end sound

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a town? What can I find there?
teach.praise: A town has markets, parks and roads, and lots of helpful people. I want to visit!
teach.nudge: What places are in a town? Who lives and works there?

learn.hook: Need a book? A train? A doctor? Every place in a town has a job!
points: We buy fruits and vegetables at the market.
We go to the hospital when we are very ill.
We borrow books from the library. We keep money safe in a bank.
We catch a train at the railway station. We post letters at the post office.

example.q: Arjun wants to read a story book but does not want to buy one. Where can he go?
steps: He wants to read, not buy.
A library lends books for some days.
So he can go to the library.

learn.reallife: Next time you go out with your family, name the places you pass.

items.q: To see a doctor when very ill?

quiz.q: Where do we go to borrow books?
quiz.explain: A library lends books. We return them after reading.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a library with a shop

quiz.q: Where can Papa keep money safe?
quiz.explain: A bank keeps people's money safe.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a bank does

quiz.q: Where are fire engines kept?
quiz.explain: Fire engines and firefighters wait at the fire station.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the fire station

quiz.q: Where do we catch a train?
quiz.explain: Trains stop at the railway station.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the bus stop and the railway station

quiz.q: Mummy needs tomatoes and onions. Where will she go?
quiz.explain: We buy vegetables at the market.
quiz.mistake: Picks a place that does not sell vegetables

quiz.q: Dadu has a very high fever. Where should he go?
quiz.explain: Doctors and nurses look after sick people at the hospital.
quiz.mistake: Does not link illness with the hospital

teach.ask: Gappu: I want a book, then a train ride! Where should I go in the town?
teach.praise: Yay! Library for books and railway station for trains. I know my town now!
teach.nudge: Which place lends books? Where do trains stop?

learn.hook: Who stitches your school uniform? Who mends your slippers? Our helpers do!
points: Community helpers do work that helps all of us.
A doctor and a nurse look after sick people.
A tailor stitches clothes. A cobbler mends shoes. A carpenter makes things from wood.
A farmer grows food. A firefighter puts out fires. A teacher helps us learn.
We should thank our helpers and treat them with respect.

example.q: The strap of Riya's sandal is broken. Who can mend it?
steps: A sandal is a kind of shoe.
A cobbler mends shoes and sandals.
So Riya should go to the cobbler.

learn.reallife: Say 'Thank you' to the guard, the bus driver and the cleaner in your school. They help you every day.

games.title: Who does what?
items: Cobblers fix shoes, sandals and bags.
A farmer grows vegetables. A tailor stitches clothes.
Teachers teach us to read, write and think.
Firefighters use water hoses to put out fires.
A carpenter works with wood. A tailor stitches clothes.

quiz.q: Who stitches clothes?
quiz.explain: A tailor uses a sewing machine to stitch clothes.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tailor and the cobbler

quiz.q: Who makes tables and chairs from wood?
quiz.explain: A carpenter works with wood.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a carpenter does

quiz.q: Who grows rice and wheat?
quiz.explain: Farmers grow crops like rice and wheat in fields.
quiz.mistake: Does not link crops with farmers

quiz.q: Who puts out fires?
quiz.explain: Firefighters come in a fire engine and put out fires.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of a firefighter

quiz.q: A little boy is lost in the market. Who can help him find his family?
quiz.explain: Police officers help people who are lost and keep us safe.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that the police help lost children

quiz.q: Who looks after sick people in a hospital with the doctor?
quiz.explain: Nurses care for sick people and help the doctor.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of a nurse

teach.ask: Gappu: Who are community helpers? Can you name some?
teach.praise: Thank you, helpers! Doctors, farmers and tailors all work hard for us!
teach.nudge: Who are the people who help us? Can you name one and say what they do?

learn.hook: Look up! Is that cloud a rabbit, a ship or an elephant?
points: The lesson 'A Show of Clouds' is about the shapes we see in clouds.
Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
The wind moves clouds and changes their shapes.
Dark grey clouds often bring rain.

example.q:
Read this.
Pari lies on the grass and looks up.
One cloud looks like a fluffy rabbit.
One looks like a big elephant.
The wind blows. The rabbit turns into a boat!
Pari laughs. 'The sky is a magic show!'
What does the rabbit cloud turn into?
steps: Find the line about the rabbit changing.
It says: 'The rabbit turns into a boat!'
So it becomes a boat.

learn.reallife: On a holiday afternoon, lie on a mat on the terrace with an adult and look for cloud shapes.

games.title: Pari's cloud show
items: The rabbit cloud turns into a boat.

games.title: Cloud facts
items: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
Clouds are made of very small water drops floating in the air.
The wind can change the shape of a cloud.
The wind pushes clouds and changes their shapes.
Clouds look fluffy like cotton, but they are made of water drops.
Dark grey clouds often bring rain.
Dark clouds are full of water and often bring rain.
In the story, Pari is scared of the clouds.
Pari laughs and calls the sky a magic show.

quiz.q: Story: 'One cloud looks like a fluffy rabbit.' What does this cloud look like?
quiz.explain: The story says the cloud looks like a fluffy rabbit.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the line carefully

quiz.q: Story: 'The wind blows. The rabbit turns into a boat!' Why does the cloud change shape?
quiz.explain: The wind blows the cloud and changes its shape.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the wind with the change

quiz.q: Story: 'Pari lies on the grass and looks up.' Where is Pari?
quiz.explain: The story says Pari lies on the grass.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from later in the story

quiz.q: Pari says, 'The sky is a magic show!' What does she mean?
options: A magician is in the sky
The clouds keep changing like magic
quiz.explain: The cloud shapes keep changing, so it feels like a magic show.
quiz.mistake: Takes the words too literally

quiz.q: Clouds are made of tiny drops of ___.
quiz.explain: Clouds are made of very small water drops.
quiz.mistake: Thinks clouds are made of something because of their colour

quiz.q: Dark grey clouds fill the sky. What will Amma most likely carry?
quiz.explain: Dark grey clouds often bring rain, so an umbrella is useful.
quiz.mistake: Does not link dark clouds with rain

teach.ask: Gappu: Why do clouds keep changing their shapes?
teach.praise: Whoosh! Clouds are tiny water drops and the wind changes their shape!
teach.nudge: What pushes the clouds around? What are clouds made of?

learn.hook: Shut your eyes and think of a pink elephant. Can you see it? That is imagination!
points: To imagine means to make a picture in your mind.
A cloud is not really an animal. We only imagine it is.
We can say a cloud 'looks like' a rabbit or 'is like' a ship.
Clues help us imagine: long ears could be a rabbit, a trunk could be an elephant.

example.q: A cloud has a long neck and four thin legs. What animal could it look like?
steps: Think of an animal with a very long neck.
A giraffe has a long neck and thin legs.
So the cloud could look like a giraffe.

learn.reallife: When you play 'house-house' or pretend a stick is a horse, you are using your imagination.

games.title: Real or imagined?
items: A cloud boat sails to the moon.
A cloud dragon sings a song.
Clouds are made of ice cream.

quiz.q: A cloud has a long curly trunk. What could it look like?
quiz.explain: An elephant has a long trunk.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue 'trunk'

quiz.q: A cloud has two long ears on top. What could it look like?
quiz.explain: A rabbit has two long ears.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue 'long ears'

quiz.q: What does 'imagine' mean?
options: To make a picture in your mind
quiz.explain: When we imagine, we make a picture in our mind.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word 'imagine'

quiz.q: Which sentence is imagined, not real?
options: A cloud lion roars at the sun.
quiz.explain: Clouds cannot roar. It is a make-believe idea.
quiz.mistake: Cannot tell real facts from make-believe

quiz.q: A cloud is long and thin like a rope. What could it look like?
quiz.explain: A snake is long and thin.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue 'long and thin'

quiz.q: Which phrase do we use to say what a cloud seems to be?
quiz.explain: We say 'The cloud looks like a ship.'
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to compare one thing with another

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend says that cloud is a dragon. But dragons are not real! How?
teach.praise: Oh! The cloud looks like a dragon. We imagine it in our mind. So fun!
teach.nudge: Is the cloud really a dragon? Or does it just look like one?

learn.hook: A cloud can be white, fluffy, big or dark. These words paint a picture!
points: Describing words tell us more about a person, animal, place or thing.
They can tell colour (white), size (big), shape (round) or feel (soft).
In 'The white cloud floats', the describing word is 'white'.
Describing words make our sentences more fun to read.

example.q: Find the describing word: 'Ravi has a big umbrella.'
steps: Ask: What kind of umbrella?
A big umbrella.
So 'big' is the describing word.

learn.reallife: When you tell Mummy 'I want the red balloon, not the blue one', you use describing words.

quiz.q: Find the describing word: 'The white cloud floats.'
quiz.explain: 'White' tells us what the cloud is like.
quiz.mistake: Picks the naming word or the doing word

quiz.q: Which one is a describing word?
quiz.explain: 'Tall' tells us what something is like.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up describing words with naming or doing words

quiz.q: Pick the best word: 'Before the rain, the clouds are ___.'
quiz.explain: Rain clouds are dark grey.
quiz.mistake: Picks a describing word that does not fit clouds

quiz.q: Find the describing word: 'The huge elephant drinks water.'
quiz.explain: 'Huge' tells us how big the elephant is.
quiz.mistake: Picks the naming word instead of the describing word

quiz.q: Describing words tell us what a person or thing is ___.
quiz.explain: Describing words tell what something is like: big, soft, red.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up describing words with doing or naming words

quiz.q: Which describing word tells about colour?
quiz.explain: Blue is a colour. Soft is feel, big is size, round is shape.
quiz.mistake: Does not tell colour words from size or shape words

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a describing word? Is 'fluffy' one?
teach.praise: Yes! 'Fluffy' tells what the cloud is like. It is a describing word!
teach.nudge: Does a describing word tell what something is like? Can you give an example?

learn.hook: Your name is the very first gift you got! Do you know what it means?
points: The lesson 'My Name' is a story about a little fly who forgets his own name. Names matter!
Every person has a name. It tells others who we are.
Many names have a meaning. Kamal means lotus. Tara means star.
Some people have a pet name too, like Chintu or Pinky.
We should say everyone's name correctly and kindly.

example.q:
Read this.
Hello! My name is Kamal.
My name means lotus.
My Dadi chose my name.
My friends call me Kamu.
I like my name very much!
Who chose Kamal's name?
steps: Find the line with 'chose'.
It says: 'My Dadi chose my name.'
So Dadi chose it.

learn.reallife: Ask your family who chose your name and what it means. It is a lovely story!

games.title: True or false? (about Kamal)
items: The passage says: 'My name means lotus.'
The passage says his Dadi chose his name.
The passage says: 'My friends call me Kamu.'
Kamal does not like his name.
He says: 'I like my name very much!'
A name tells others who we are.
When people hear our name, they know who we are.

quiz.q: Passage: 'Hello! My name is Kamal.' What is the child's name?
quiz.explain: The child says, 'My name is Kamal.'
quiz.mistake: Picks the pet name or another word from the passage

quiz.q: Passage: 'My name means lotus.' What does the name Kamal mean?
quiz.explain: The passage says Kamal means lotus.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up meanings of different names

quiz.q: Passage: 'My friends call me Kamu.' What is 'Kamu'?
quiz.explain: Kamu is a short, loving name his friends use. It is a pet name.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a pet name is

quiz.q: A new friend says your name the wrong way. What is a kind thing to do?
options: Tell them gently how to say it
quiz.explain: Gently showing them helps them learn your name.
quiz.mistake: Reacts in an unkind way

quiz.q: Why do we have names?
options: So others know who we are
quiz.explain: Names help people know and call each one of us.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand what a name is for

quiz.q: The name Tara means ___.
quiz.explain: Tara means star.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the meanings of names

teach.ask: Gappu: Why do people have names? Do names mean anything?
teach.praise: I love it! A name tells who we are, and many names have a lovely meaning!
teach.nudge: How do names help other people? Do some names have a meaning?

learn.hook: Names are special, so they wear a crown: a capital letter!
points: Names of people begin with a capital letter: Riya, Kabir, Asha.
Names of places begin with a capital letter too: Delhi, Pune, India.
The word I is always a capital letter.
Other words like cat, tree and ball do not need a capital letter in the middle of a sentence.

example.q: Fix the names: 'meena lives in jaipur.'
steps: meena is a person's name → Meena.
jaipur is a place's name → Jaipur.
Meena is also the first word, so it needs a capital anyway.

learn.reallife: Look at the name on your notebook cover. It starts with a capital letter!

games.title: Capital letter rules
items: Names of people begin with a capital letter.
Names of places begin with a capital letter.
The word 'I' is written as a small letter.
The word I is always a capital letter.
'mango' needs a capital letter in the middle of a sentence.
Mango is not a name of a person or place.
It is a place name and starts with a capital D.

quiz.q: Which name is written correctly?
quiz.explain: A person's name begins with a capital letter. Only Riya does.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that names begin with a capital letter

quiz.q: Which word needs a capital letter? 'I play with sonu.'
quiz.explain: Sonu is a person's name, so it needs a capital S.
quiz.mistake: Does not spot the name in the sentence

quiz.q: Which place name is written correctly?
quiz.explain: Place names begin with a capital letter. Mumbai has a capital M.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only people's names need capital letters

quiz.q: Why does 'Ravi' begin with a capital R?
quiz.explain: Names of people always begin with a capital letter.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the rule for names

quiz.q: In which sentence are all the capital letters right?
quiz.explain: Asha and Pune are names, and both have capital letters. The sentence starts with a capital too.
quiz.mistake: Misses a small letter in one of the names

quiz.q: The word 'I' is always written as ___.
quiz.explain: 'I' is always a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence.
quiz.mistake: Writes 'i' as a small letter

teach.ask: Gappu: I wrote 'my friend is ravi.' My teacher circled 'ravi'. Why?
teach.praise: Oh! Ravi is a name, so it needs a capital R. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What kind of word is 'ravi'? How should names begin?

learn.hook: K-A-B-I-R! Can you spell your name like a spelling champion?
points: We spell a name by saying its letters one by one: R-A-V-I.
Count the letters to check your spelling. Ravi has 4 letters.
Names can be put in ABC order by their first letter.
Write your own name with care, with a capital letter first.

example.q: Put these names in ABC order: Chetan, Anu, Bina.
steps: Look at the first letters: C, A, B.
In the alphabet, A comes first, then B, then C.
So: Anu, Bina, Chetan.

learn.reallife: Your class register lists names in ABC order. That is why Aarav is called before Zoya!

games.title: ABC order
games.prompt: Put the names in ABC order

quiz.q: How many letters are in the name 'Meena'?
quiz.explain: M-e-e-n-a. That is 5 letters.
quiz.mistake: Counts the double e as one letter

quiz.q: Which name begins with the letter S?
quiz.explain: Sonu begins with S.
quiz.mistake: Does not look at the first letter

quiz.q: Which name comes first in ABC order?
quiz.explain: Anil begins with A. A comes first in the alphabet.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the first letters

quiz.q: Ravi spells his name aloud. Which is right?
quiz.explain: Ravi is spelt R-A-V-I.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of letters

quiz.q: What is the last letter of the name 'Kabir'?
quiz.explain: K-a-b-i-r. The last letter is r.
quiz.mistake: Picks the first letter instead of the last

quiz.q: How many letters are in the name 'Zoya'?
quiz.explain: Z-o-y-a. That is 4 letters.
quiz.mistake: Counts carelessly

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I spell my name? And how do I know it is right?
teach.praise: G-A-P-P-U! I say each letter, start with a capital and count the letters!
teach.nudge: Do I say the letters one by one? How does a name begin?

learn.hook: Caw, caw! Who is that on the wall every morning?
points: The lesson 'The Crow' is about a bird we see almost every day.
A crow is mostly black. It has a strong beak.
It says 'caw, caw'. It eats grains, fruits, insects and leftover food.
Crows make nests of twigs in trees. They often live in groups.
Crows are very clever birds. By eating scraps, they help keep places clean.

example.q:
Read this.
Kaalu the crow sits on the wall.
'Caw, caw!' he calls in the morning.
He is black and shiny, with a strong beak.
He eats grains, fruits and bits of roti.
He makes a nest of twigs in the neem tree.
Kaalu is a very clever bird!
Where does Kaalu sit?
steps: Look at the first line.
It says: 'Kaalu the crow sits on the wall.'
So he sits on the wall.

learn.reallife: Look out of your window in the morning. You may see crows on the wall or on a tree.

games.title: Crow facts
items: That is the sound a crow makes.
Most of a crow's feathers are black.
Crows build nests with small sticks called twigs.
A crow is a bird. Birds have two legs.
Crows are known to be smart birds.
Crows live on land and fly in the air. They make nests in trees.

quiz.q: Passage: "'Caw, caw!' he calls in the morning." What sound does the crow make?
quiz.explain: The passage says Kaalu calls 'Caw, caw!'
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the sounds of different birds

quiz.q: Passage: 'He makes a nest of twigs in the neem tree.' What is the nest made of?
quiz.explain: The passage says the nest is made of twigs.
quiz.mistake: Does not read what the nest is made of

quiz.q: Passage: 'He eats grains, fruits and bits of roti.' Which food is NOT in this line?
quiz.explain: The line names grains, fruits and roti. Ice cream is not there.
quiz.mistake: Does not check each food in the line

quiz.q: Passage: 'He makes a nest of twigs in the neem tree.' Where is Kaalu's nest?
quiz.explain: The passage says the nest is in the neem tree.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a place without reading

quiz.q: Passage: 'Kaalu is a very clever bird!' Which word tells us Kaalu is smart?
quiz.explain: 'Clever' means smart.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'clever'

quiz.q: Passage: 'He is black and shiny, with a strong beak.' What colour is Kaalu?
quiz.explain: The passage says he is black and shiny.
quiz.mistake: Picks a colour without reading the line

teach.ask: Gappu: A black bird keeps calling outside my window. Tell me about crows!
teach.praise: Caw caw! The crow is black, clever and makes a nest of twigs. Now I know!
teach.nudge: What sound does a crow make? What colour is it? What does it eat?

learn.hook: Everything has a name: you, your dog, your school and your pencil!
points: A naming word is the name of a person, animal, place or thing.
Person: Ravi, teacher. Animal: crow, cow. Place: school, Delhi. Thing: pen, cup.
In 'The crow sits on the wall', crow and wall are naming words.
Naming words answer 'Who?' or 'What?'

example.q: Find the naming words: 'Meena feeds the crow.'
steps: Who feeds? Meena. That is a person.
Feeds what? The crow. That is an animal.
'feeds' is a doing word.

learn.reallife: When you make a shopping list for Mummy, like milk, bread and eggs, you write naming words!

quiz.q: Which one is a naming word?
quiz.explain: 'Crow' is the name of an animal.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up naming words with doing or describing words

quiz.q: Find the naming word: 'The crow sits on the wall.'
quiz.explain: 'Crow' names an animal. (Wall is a naming word too.)
quiz.mistake: Picks the doing word 'sits'

quiz.q: Which naming word is the name of a place?
quiz.explain: A school is a place. Ravi is a person, crow an animal, pen a thing.
quiz.mistake: Does not tell places from people or things

quiz.q: Which naming word is the name of an animal?
quiz.explain: A tiger is an animal.
quiz.mistake: Does not tell animals from people, places or things

quiz.q: How many naming words are in 'The cat drinks milk.'?
quiz.explain: cat and milk are naming words. 'drinks' is a doing word.
quiz.mistake: Counts every word as a naming word

quiz.q: Naming words are names of people, animals, places and ___.
quiz.explain: Naming words name people, animals, places and things.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up naming words with doing or describing words

teach.ask: Gappu: My teacher says 'crow' is a naming word. What is a naming word?
teach.praise: Caw! A naming word is the name of a person, animal, place or thing!
teach.nudge: What does a naming word tell us? Is it a name of a person, animal, place or thing?

learn.hook: One crow on the wall... then five crows! How do we say 'many'?
points: One means just one. Many means more than one.
Add -s to many words: crow → crows, nest → nests, tree → trees.
Add -es to words ending in s, x, ch or sh: bus → buses, box → boxes.
Use the 'many' word when there is more than one: 'three crows'.

example.q: One box. Two ___.
steps: box ends with x.
For words ending in x, we add -es.
box → boxes.

learn.reallife: At the fruit shop you say 'one banana' but 'six bananas'.

quiz.q: One crow, many ___.
quiz.explain: We add -s to crow to make crows.
quiz.mistake: Adds -es where only -s is needed

quiz.q: One box, many ___.
quiz.explain: Box ends with x, so we add -es: boxes.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in x

quiz.q: One bus, two ___.
quiz.explain: Bus ends with s, so we add -es: buses.
quiz.mistake: Does not add -es to a word ending in s

quiz.q: Which is the right word? 'I see three ___ on the wall.'
quiz.explain: Three means more than one, so we say crows.
quiz.mistake: Uses the 'one' word for more than one

quiz.q: Which word is for just ONE thing?
quiz.explain: 'Tree' is one. trees, birds and cups mean many.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the -s that means many

quiz.q: One dish, many ___.
quiz.explain: Dish ends with sh, so we add -es: dishes.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in sh

teach.ask: Gappu: I saw one crow, then lots more came! How do I say more than one?
teach.praise: Yes! One crow, many crows. We add -s to show more than one!
teach.nudge: What do I add to 'crow' when there are many?

learn.hook: A monkey on a crocodile's back in the middle of a river! How will he escape?
points: In the lesson 'The Smart Monkey', a monkey is wiser than people think. Here we read another smart-monkey tale: an old Indian folk tale about a monkey and a crocodile.
A folk tale is a story told by grandparents to children for many, many years.
In this tale, a clever monkey uses his brain to stay safe.
Read the story in order: beginning, middle and end.

example.q:
Read this story.
A monkey lived in a jamun tree by a river.
He gave sweet jamuns to his friend, the crocodile.
The crocodile said, 'Sit on my back. Come to my home.'
In the river, he said, 'My wife wants to eat a monkey's heart!'
The monkey stayed calm. 'I left my heart in the tree! Let's go back.'
At the tree, the monkey jumped up to a high branch. He was safe!
How did the monkey get back to the tree?
steps: The monkey said his heart was in the tree.
The crocodile believed him and swam back.
So the monkey used a clever trick.
example.answer: He tricked the crocodile into taking him back.

learn.reallife: Ask your Dadi or Nani to tell you a folk tale. Many of them have clever animals!

games.title: Story in order
items: The monkey gives jamuns to the crocodile.
The monkey sits on the crocodile's back.
The crocodile tells about his wife's wish.
The monkey says his heart is in the tree.
The monkey jumps up to a high branch.

games.title: True or false? (about the story)
items: In the story, the monkey lived in a jamun tree.
The story says: 'A monkey lived in a jamun tree by a river.'
In the story, the monkey cried and gave up.
The monkey stayed calm and thought of a trick.
In the story, the monkey really left his heart in the tree.
It was a trick. He said it to get back to the tree.
In the story, the monkey was safe at the end.
He jumped up to a high branch. He was safe!
In the story, the crocodile carried the monkey on his back.
The crocodile said, 'Sit on my back.'

quiz.q: Story: 'A monkey lived in a jamun tree by a river.' Where did the monkey live?
quiz.explain: The story says he lived in a jamun tree by a river.
quiz.mistake: Picks the river because it is in the same line

quiz.q: Story: 'He gave sweet jamuns to his friend, the crocodile.' What did the monkey give?
quiz.explain: The story says the monkey gave sweet jamuns.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a fruit monkeys usually eat

quiz.q: Story: 'Sit on my back. Come to my home.' How did the monkey go into the river?
quiz.explain: The crocodile asked the monkey to sit on his back.
quiz.mistake: Does not read who is speaking and what he offers

quiz.q: The monkey said, 'I left my heart in the tree!' Why did he say this?
options: It was a trick to get back safely
quiz.explain: Nobody can leave their heart behind. It was a clever trick.
quiz.mistake: Believes the trick, like the crocodile did

quiz.q: Story: 'At the tree, the monkey jumped up to a high branch.' How did the story end?
options: The monkey fell in the river
quiz.explain: The story ends with: 'He was safe!'
quiz.mistake: Does not read the last line

quiz.q: At the start of the story, the monkey and the crocodile were ___.
quiz.explain: The monkey gave jamuns to 'his friend, the crocodile'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks about the end of the story instead of the start

teach.ask: Gappu: How did the little monkey escape from the big crocodile?
teach.praise: So smart! He stayed calm and said his heart was in the tree. What a trick!
teach.nudge: What did the monkey say about his heart? Was he calm or scared?

learn.hook: When trouble comes, don't panic! Think like the smart monkey.
points: Presence of mind means staying calm and thinking quickly in trouble.
The monkey did not cry. He thought of a plan.
If you are in trouble, stop, take a deep breath and think.
Ask a trusted adult for help: a parent, a teacher or a police officer.

example.q: Arya gets lost in a crowded mela. What should she do?
steps: Stop and stay calm. Do not run about.
Find a police officer or a helper at the mela.
Tell them her name and her parent's phone number.
example.answer: Stay calm and ask a police officer or mela helper for help.

learn.reallife: Learn your parent's phone number by heart. It helps if you are ever lost.

games.title: Smart or not smart in trouble?
Keep a cool head
items: Presence of mind means staying calm and thinking fast.
That is exactly what it means.
The monkey showed presence of mind.
He stayed calm and thought of a trick.
If you are lost, you should go with any stranger.
Ask a police officer or a shop helper. Never go off with a stranger.
Taking a deep breath can help you stay calm.
Slow breathing helps us calm down and think.
When a friend gets hurt, it is best to run away.
Stay calm and call an adult to help.

quiz.q: What does 'presence of mind' mean?
quiz.explain: It means you keep calm and think fast when there is trouble.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the phrase 'presence of mind'

quiz.q: How did the monkey show presence of mind?
options: He stayed calm and thought of a trick
quiz.explain: He kept calm and quickly made up a clever plan.
quiz.mistake: Does not link presence of mind with the monkey's trick

quiz.q: You are lost in a big market. What is a smart thing to do?
options: Stay calm and ask a police officer
quiz.explain: A police officer can help you find your family safely.
quiz.mistake: Panics or trusts a stranger

quiz.q: Your friend falls and hurts her knee in the park. What should you do first?
options: Stay calm and call an adult
quiz.explain: An adult can help clean and treat the hurt knee.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to act calmly in trouble

quiz.q: Which word means the same as 'calm'?
quiz.explain: Calm means quiet and peaceful, not upset.
quiz.mistake: Picks a feeling that is the opposite of calm

quiz.q: Which helps most when you are in trouble?
quiz.explain: A calm mind can think of a good plan, like the smart monkey did.
quiz.mistake: Thinks panicking helps

teach.ask: Gappu: What is 'presence of mind'? I always panic when something goes wrong!
teach.praise: Phew! Stay calm and think fast, just like the smart monkey. I can do that!
teach.nudge: Should I panic or stay calm? What should I do with my brain?

learn.hook: Clever or foolish? High or low? Let's play with words from the story!
points: Clever means smart. The opposite of clever is foolish.
A river bank is the land at the side of a river.
The monkey jumped up to a high branch. The opposite of high is low.
The monkey was safe. The opposite of safe is in danger.

example.q: The monkey was clever. The crocodile believed a silly trick. Which word fits the crocodile: clever or foolish?
steps: The crocodile believed the monkey's heart was in the tree.
That was not smart.
So the crocodile was foolish.

learn.reallife: When you play 'opposites' with your friends, you use pairs like high – low and sweet – sour.

items.text: The jamun tree stood on the ___ of the river.
The monkey jumped to a ___ branch.

quiz.q: The jamun tree is on the bank of the river. What is a river bank?
options: Land at the side of a river
quiz.explain: The bank of a river is the land along its side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'bank' only means a place for money

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'clever'?
quiz.explain: Clever means smart. Foolish means not smart.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with the same meaning

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'high'?
quiz.explain: A high branch is far up. Low means near the ground.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that means almost the same as high

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'sweet'?
quiz.explain: Sweet like sugar, sour like a lemon.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that is not about taste

quiz.q: Which word means 'smart'?
quiz.explain: Clever and smart mean the same.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'clever'

quiz.q: Where does a crocodile live?
options: In rivers and on their banks
quiz.explain: Crocodiles swim in rivers and lakes and rest on the banks.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up where different animals live

teach.ask: Gappu: The monkey was clever. What is the opposite of clever?
teach.praise: Right! Clever and foolish are opposites. The crocodile was foolish!
teach.nudge: What do we call someone who is not clever? What is the opposite word?

learn.hook: One drop is tiny. But many drops can fill a bucket! How?
points: The lesson 'Little Drops of Water' is a poem. It shows that small things add up to big things.
Many little drops make a bucket full of water.
Many small good deeds make the world a kinder place.
'Little by little' means slowly, a small bit at a time.

example.q:
Read this poem.
One little drop goes plip, plop, plip,
Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.
Drop after drop, it fills up high,
Enough for my plants when they are dry.
Little by little, small things grow
Into big things. Now you know!
What fills up the bucket?
steps: The poem says 'Drop after drop, it fills up high'.
So many small drops fill the bucket.

learn.reallife: Putting one coin in your piggy bank every day adds up to a lot of coins!

games.title: True or false? (about the poem)
items: In the poem, the drops fall into a bucket.
The poem says: 'Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.'
In the poem, one drop fills the whole bucket.
It is 'drop after drop' that fills the bucket.
In the poem, the water is for the plants.
The poem says: 'Enough for my plants when they are dry.'
The poem says small things can add up to big things.
It says: 'Little by little, small things grow into big things.'
In the poem, the bucket stays empty.

games.title: Small to big
games.prompt: Put these from smallest to biggest

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.' Where do the drops fall?
quiz.explain: The line says the drops fall into my bucket.
quiz.mistake: Does not read where the drops fall

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Drop after drop, it fills up high.' What happens to the bucket?
quiz.explain: Drop after drop, the bucket fills up high.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand 'fills up high'

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Enough for my plants when they are dry.' Who will get the water?
quiz.explain: The water is enough for the dry plants.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without reading the line

quiz.q: 'Little by little, small things grow into big things.' What does this mean?
options: Many small bits together make something big
quiz.explain: Small drops or small steps, added up, become big.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the main idea of the poem

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'high'?
quiz.explain: high and dry both end with the 'eye' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from the poem that does not sound the same at the end

quiz.q: Ria puts 1 coin in her piggy bank every day for 10 days. How many coins does she have?
quiz.explain: 1 coin each day for 10 days makes 10 coins. Small things add up!
quiz.mistake: Counts only one day

teach.ask: Gappu: One drop is so tiny! How can drops ever fill a bucket?
teach.praise: Wow! Drop after drop, many little drops add up and fill the bucket!
teach.nudge: Is it one drop or many drops? What happens when they come together?

learn.hook: Every drop counts! Can you be a Water Hero today?
points: All living things need water. Clean water is precious.
Most water on Earth is salty sea water. We cannot drink it.
Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Tell an adult about a leaking tap so it can be fixed.
Use the water from washing vegetables to water the plants.

example.q: Kabir leaves the tap running while he brushes his teeth. What should he do?
steps: Running water goes down the drain and is wasted.
He needs water only to wet the brush and rinse.
So he should turn off the tap while brushing.
example.answer: Turn off the tap while brushing.

learn.reallife: Some homes and schools in India collect rainwater on the roof and store it to use later.

games.title: Water Hero or Water Waster?
items: turning off the tap while brushing
watering plants with used vegetable water
playing with a water pipe for fun
throwing away half a glass of drinking water
washing a car with a running pipe

games.title: Water facts
items: Plants, animals and people all need water to live.
Most water on Earth is salty sea water.
Most of Earth's water is in the seas and oceans. It is salty.
Drip by drip, a leaking tap wastes a lot of water.
We can drink sea water when we are thirsty.
Sea water is too salty to drink.
It is fine to leave the tap running while brushing.
That wastes a lot of water. Turn it off.

quiz.q: What should you do while brushing your teeth?
quiz.explain: Turning off the tap saves the water that would go down the drain.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that running water is wasted

quiz.q: A tap at school is leaking. What should you do?
options: Tell a teacher so it can be fixed
quiz.explain: A leaking tap wastes water. A grown-up can get it fixed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a small leak does not matter

options: Wash the car with a pipe
quiz.explain: Plants can use the water. It is not wasted.
quiz.mistake: Does not think of reusing water

quiz.q: Most of the water on Earth is in the ___.
